ei.title: New Challenges: Space: The Final Frontier
ei.subject: 공통영어2

fullPassage: The need to explore new frontiers like the Arctic and the American West may have been sparked by curiosity, but a major reason was to discover new resources. Without new resources and technology, the Industrial Revolution of the 19th century would not have led to the rise of new industries and the growth of cities. In the late 20th century, the Information Technology Revolution connected the world and transformed economies. Now, it seems that space is the latest frontier for entrepreneurs to explore. Finding new resources and exploring the unique environment are new opportunities for those who dare to take up the challenge. The solar system is composed of many rocks floating in space. The large ones are called planets, and the smaller ones are called asteroids. Research has shown that asteroids contain valuable resources like gold and rare earth elements. For example, one asteroid, 16 Psyche, is reported to consist mainly of gold and other precious metals, whose value is equal to billions of dollars per person on Earth. From a space explorers' perspective, however, the most valuable resources from asteroids are neither valuable precious metals nor rare mineral deposits. That valuable resource could actually be water, and it seems to have been overlooked because it doesn't seem as exciting as gold. Water is expensive to transport into space due to its weight and volume. Having a space station with sufficient water supplies in orbit around Earth would make space explorations much easier. No one knows for sure what asteroid mining will look like, but it seems that robotic mining is most likely. Robots will be sent to dig for target materials and send them back towards Earth. They will be programmed to explore the surface and identify materials, and be equipped for tasks such as drilling, collecting, and transporting. They may work independently or be controlled remotely from Earth. Unfortunately, these types of robots have yet to be developed since the technology is still young. As technology continues to develop, better methods for obtaining materials will undoubtedly emerge. Being on the International Space Station (ISS) is a unique experience. Astronauts live and work in microgravity, floating around instead of walking. Researchers get to see Earth from a completely new perspective, and they get to work on important scientific research in conditions that are different from Earth's. Many manufacturers are interested in manufacturing in space because the quality of a lot of products manufactured on Earth is influenced by temperature, pressure, radiation, and even the effects of gravity. Creating good conditions for certain types of manufacturing on Earth requires the use of a lot of energy and resources, but those conditions occur naturally in space. Drugs, beauty and food products, and advanced materials are all potential candidates to be tested and produced in space. For example, without the effects of gravity, products that require a uniform quality like cosmetics would be easier to mix. Other materials like 3D printed skin or muscle benefit from low pressure and gravity too. Although the sun's radiation can be unhealthy for our skin, getting away from the protective effects of the atmosphere could also benefit the testing of products. For example, fabrics and skin creams could be tested for their ability to protect against solar radiation. Also, semiconductors and glass communication cables could be produced with higher purity and fewer faults. Space technology has advanced greatly, and it seems that the cost of running a space program and improving it has decreased substantially since ambitious entrepreneurs have joined the adventure. The conditions in space open up the possibility of manufacturing newer and better products. Challenges remain, but it's not unreasonable to imagine sending a message from a device equipped with semiconductors that were produced in space. The space project will ultimately reach a point where adventurous minds and their technological innovations will be able to travel safely to stars beyond the solar system. The resources required to drive economic activity that have existed far beyond the reach of humanity are becoming much more reachable. The question is no longer about how; it's about when.

questions.passage: Research has ①<u>shown</u> that asteroids contain valuable resources like gold and rare earth elements.  For example, one asteroid, 16 Psyche, is reported to consist mainly of gold and other precious metals, ②<u>which</u> value is equal to billions of dollars per person on Earth.  From a space explorers' perspective, however, the most valuable resources from asteroids are neither valuable precious metals ③<u>nor</u> rare mineral deposits.  That valuable resource could actually be water, and it seems to have been overlooked because it doesn't seem as ④<u>exciting</u> as gold.  Water is expensive to transport into space due to its weight and volume.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② which → whose (소유격 관계대명사)
det.analysis:
① shown: 'Research has shown that ~'은 'have/has + 과거분사'의 현재완료라 shown이 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

② which → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 'gold and other precious metals, ②___ value is equal to billions'에서 뒤에 바로 명사 value가 이어져요. 즉 '그 금속들의 가치'처럼 '~의'라는 소유 관계이므로 소유격 관계대명사 whose(그런데 그것의)가 와야 해요. which는 소유 관계를 나타낼 수 없어서, 바로 뒤에 명사가 올 수 없어요. ❌ ←정답

③ nor: 'neither A nor B(A도 B도 아닌)' 상관접속사라 nor가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

④ exciting: 'as exciting as gold(금만큼 흥미로운)'에서 사물(물)이 흥미로움을 '주는' 쪽이라 능동의 -ing형 exciting이 맞아요. ✅ 올바름
det.tip: 뒤에 명사(value)가 바로 오고 '~의'로 해석되면 소유격 관계대명사 whose → metals, whose value(금속들, 그리고 그것들의 가치)

questions.passage: Space technology has advanced greatly, and it seems that the cost of running a space program and improving it has decreased substantially since ambitious entrepreneurs have joined the adventure.  The conditions in space open up the possibility of manufacturing newer and better products.  Challenges remain, but it's not unreasonable to ①<u>imagine</u> sending a message from a device equipped with semiconductors that ②<u>was</u> produced in space.  The space project will ultimately reach a point where adventurous minds and their technological innovations will be ③<u>able</u> to travel safely to stars beyond the solar system.  The resources required to drive economic activity that have ④<u>existed</u> far beyond the reach of humanity are becoming much more reachable.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② was → were (복수 선행사 semiconductors)
det.analysis:
① imagine: 'imagine sending a message'에서 imagine은 뒤에 동명사(-ing)를 목적어로 취하므로 sending을 받는 imagine이 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

② was → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 'semiconductors that ②___ produced in space'는 '우주에서 생산된 반도체'라는 뜻이에요. 관계대명사 that이 가리키는 선행사가 복수형 semiconductors(반도체들)이므로 be동사도 복수형 were가 되어야 해요. 단수 was는 수일치가 틀려요. ❌ ←정답

③ able: 'will be able to travel'은 'be able to + 동사원형(~할 수 있다)' 구조라 able이 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

④ existed: 'resources ~ that have existed far beyond the reach'는 'have + 과거분사'의 현재완료라 existed가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름
det.tip: 관계대명사절의 동사는 선행사에 수일치 → semiconductors(복수) that were produced(생산된 반도체들)

questions.passage: For example, without the effects of gravity, products that ①<u>require</u> a uniform quality like cosmetics would be easier to mix.  Other materials like 3D ②<u>printed</u> skin or muscle benefit from low pressure and gravity too.  Although the sun's radiation can be unhealthy for our skin, ③<u>get</u> away from the protective effects of the atmosphere could also benefit the testing of products.  For example, fabrics and skin creams could be tested for their ability to protect against solar radiation.  Also, semiconductors and glass communication cables could be produced with higher purity and ④<u>fewer</u> faults.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ get → getting (동명사 주어)
det.analysis:
① require: 'products that ①require a uniform quality'에서 관계대명사 that의 선행사가 복수형 products(제품들)이므로 동사도 복수형 require가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

② printed: 'materials like 3D printed skin'에서 '3D로 프린팅된 피부'라는 뜻으로 명사 skin을 꾸미는 과거분사 printed가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

③ get → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! '③___ away from the protective effects of the atmosphere could also benefit the testing'에서 문장의 주어 자리예요. 동사가 주어로 오려면 동명사(-ing)가 되어야 하고, 뒤의 단수동사 could와 호응하므로 Getting(벗어나는 것)이 되어야 해요. 동사원형 get은 주어가 될 수 없어 틀려요. ❌ ←정답

④ fewer: 'fewer faults(더 적은 결함)'에서 faults는 셀 수 있는 명사라 fewer가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름
det.tip: 동사가 주어 자리에 오면 동명사(-ing) → Getting away ~ could benefit(벗어나는 것이 ~에 도움이 될 수 있다)

questions.passage: The need to explore new frontiers like the Arctic and the American West may have been sparked by ①<u>curiosity</u>, but a major reason was to discover new resources.  Without new resources and technology, the Industrial Revolution of the 19th century would not have led to the ②<u>fall</u> of new industries and the growth of cities.  In the late 20th century, the Information Technology Revolution connected the world and transformed economies.  Now, it seems that space is the latest frontier for entrepreneurs to explore.  Finding new resources and exploring the unique environment are new ③<u>opportunities</u> for those who ④<u>dare</u> to take up the challenge.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ② fall → rise: 산업 혁명이 새 산업의 '등장(rise)'을 이끌었다
det.analysis:
✅ ① curiosity(호기심): 새 개척지 탐험이 '호기심'에서 촉발되었을 수 있다는 문맥에 적절해요

❌ ② fall(쇠퇴) → rise(등장, 부상): '새 자원과 기술이 없었다면 산업 혁명이 새 산업의 등장(rise)과 도시 성장을 이끌지 못했을 것'이라는 문맥이에요. 산업 혁명이 새 산업의 '쇠퇴(fall)'를 이끌었다는 것은 정반대예요 ← 정답

✅ ③ opportunities(기회): 자원 발견과 환경 탐사가 새로운 '기회'라는 문맥에 적절해요

✅ ④ dare(감히 ~하다): '감히' 도전에 나서는 사람들이라는 문맥에 적절해요
det.tip: the rise of new industries(새 산업의 등장) ↔ fall(쇠퇴)

questions.passage: No one knows for sure what asteroid mining will look like, but it seems that robotic mining is most likely.  Robots will be sent to ①<u>dig</u> for target materials and send them back towards Earth.  They will be programmed to explore the surface and identify materials, and be equipped for tasks such as ②<u>drilling</u>, collecting, and transporting.  They may work independently or be controlled remotely from Earth.  Unfortunately, these types of robots have yet to be developed since the technology is still ③<u>old</u>.  As technology continues to develop, better methods for obtaining materials will undoubtedly ④<u>emerge</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ old → young: 기술이 아직 '초기(young)'라서
det.analysis:
✅ ① dig(파다): 로봇이 목표 물질을 '파내기' 위해 보내진다는 문맥에 적절해요

✅ ② drilling(구멍 뚫기): 로봇이 뚫기, 수집, 운반 같은 작업을 위해 장비를 갖춘다는 문맥에 적절해요

❌ ③ old(오래된) → young(초기의, 역사가 짧은): '이런 로봇은 기술이 아직 초기(young)라서 개발되지 못했다'는 문맥이에요. 기술이 '오래되었다(old)'면 이미 개발되었을 것이므로 정반대예요 ← 정답

✅ ④ emerge(나타나다): 기술이 발전하면서 더 나은 방법이 '나타날' 것이라는 문맥에 적절해요
det.tip: the technology is still young(기술이 아직 초기이다) ↔ old(오래된)

questions.passage: Space technology has advanced greatly, and it seems that the cost of running a space program and improving it has decreased substantially since ambitious entrepreneurs have joined the adventure.  The conditions in space open up the possibility of manufacturing newer and better products.  Challenges remain, but it's not unreasonable to imagine sending a message from a device equipped with semiconductors that were produced in space.  The space project will ultimately reach a point where adventurous minds and their technological innovations will be able to travel safely to stars beyond the solar system.  The resources required to drive economic activity that have existed far __________ are becoming much more reachable.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸에 beyond the reach of humanity(인류의 손이 닿지 않는 곳에)가 적절
det.analysis:
✅ ① beyond the reach of humanity(인류의 손이 닿지 않는 곳에): 'The resources ~ that have existed far ___ are becoming much more reachable'에서 뒤의 '점점 더 도달 가능해지고 있다(more reachable)'와 대조를 이루려면, 그 자원이 지금껏 '인류의 손이 닿지 않는 곳에' 있었다는 뜻이 되어야 해요 ← 정답

❌ ② within everyone's easy grasp(누구나 쉽게 닿는 곳에): 이미 닿는 곳에 있었다면 '더 도달 가능해진다'는 흐름과 모순돼요

❌ ③ close to major cities(대도시 근처에): 우주 자원과 관련 없는 내용이에요

❌ ④ hidden inside the Earth(지구 속에 숨겨진): 우주의 자원을 말하는 문맥과 맞지 않아요
det.tip: far ___ ↔ becoming much more reachable(더 도달 가능해지는) → beyond the reach of humanity(인류의 손이 닿지 않는 곳에)

questions.passage: Being on the International Space Station (ISS) is a unique experience.  Astronauts live and work in microgravity, floating around instead of walking.  Researchers get to see Earth from a completely new perspective, and they get to work on important scientific research in conditions that are different from Earth's.  Many manufacturers are interested in manufacturing in space because the quality of a lot of products manufactured on Earth is influenced by temperature, pressure, radiation, and even __________.  Creating good conditions for certain types of manufacturing on Earth requires the use of a lot of energy and resources, but those conditions occur naturally in space.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸에 the effects of gravity(중력의 영향)가 적절
det.analysis:
❌ ① the passage of time(시간의 흐름): 제품 품질에 영향을 주는 물리적 요인 나열과 어울리지 않아요

❌ ② the price of fuel(연료 가격): 제조 조건이 아니라 비용이라 문맥에 맞지 않아요

❌ ③ the color of light(빛의 색): 품질에 영향을 주는 요인으로 언급되지 않았어요

✅ ④ the effects of gravity(중력의 영향): '제품 품질은 온도, 압력, 방사선, 그리고 심지어 ___의 영향을 받는다'에서 우주 제조의 핵심 주제인 '중력의 영향'이 나열의 마지막에 오는 것이 자연스러워요 ← 정답
det.tip: temperature, pressure, radiation, and even ___ → the effects of gravity(중력의 영향)

questions.passage: No one knows for sure what asteroid mining will look like, but it seems that robotic mining is most likely.  Robots will be sent to dig for target materials and send them back towards Earth.  They will be programmed to explore the surface and identify materials, and be equipped for tasks such as drilling, collecting, and transporting.  They may work independently or be controlled remotely from Earth.  Unfortunately, these types of robots have yet to be developed since the technology is still young.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: 소행성 채굴 로봇의 작동 방식.
det.analysis:
① 본문 'Robots will be sent to dig for target materials and send them back towards Earth'와 일치해요

② 본문 'They will be programmed to explore the surface and identify materials'와 일치해요

③ 본문 'They may work independently or be controlled remotely from Earth'에서 로봇은 '독립적으로 작동하거나(or)' 원격 제어될 수 있다고 했어요. '오직 원격으로만 제어되며 독립 작동할 수 없다'는 반대이므로 불일치예요 ← 정답

④ 본문 'these types of robots have yet to be developed since the technology is still young'과 일치해요
det.tip: work independently OR be controlled remotely(독립 작동 또는 원격 제어) — '오직 원격으로만'이 아닙니다.

ch: 로봇은 목표 물질을 파내어 지구로 돌려보내도록 보내질 것이다.
로봇은 표면을 탐사하고 물질을 식별하도록 프로그래밍될 것이다.
로봇은 오직 지구에서 원격으로만 제어되며 독립적으로는 작동할 수 없다.
이런 유형의 로봇은 기술이 아직 초기라 아직 개발되지 않았다.

questions.passage: The need to explore new frontiers like the Arctic and the American West may have been sparked by curiosity, but a major reason was to discover new resources.  Without new resources and technology, the Industrial Revolution of the 19th century would not have led to the rise of new industries and the growth of cities.  In the late 20th century, the Information Technology Revolution connected the world and transformed economies.  Now, it seems that space is the latest frontier for entrepreneurs to explore.  Finding new resources and exploring the unique environment are new opportunities for those who dare to take up the challenge.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: 개척지 탐험의 역사와 우주.
det.analysis:
① 본문 'In the late 20th century, the Information Technology Revolution connected the world'에서 정보기술 혁명은 '20세기 후반'이었어요. '19세기'는 산업 혁명의 시기라 시기가 뒤바뀌어 불일치예요

② 본문 'Without new resources and technology, the Industrial Revolution ~ would not have led to the rise of new industries and the growth of cities'와 일치해요 ← 정답

③ 본문 'may have been sparked by curiosity, but a major reason was to discover new resources'에서 호기심 '뿐만 아니라' 자원 발견이 주된 이유였어요. '오로지 호기심 때문'은 불일치예요

④ 본문 'space is the latest frontier for entrepreneurs to explore'에서 '기업가'가 탐사한다고 했으므로 '정부 기관만'은 불일치예요
det.tip: Without ~ would not have led to the rise(~이 없었다면 등장을 이끌지 못했을 것) 문장이 일치합니다.

ch: 정보기술 혁명은 19세기에 세계를 연결하고 경제를 변화시켰다.
새 자원과 기술이 없었다면 산업 혁명은 새 산업과 도시 성장을 이끌지 못했을 것이다.
북극과 미국 서부 탐험은 오로지 호기심 때문에 이루어졌다.
이제 우주는 정부 기관만이 탐사할 수 있는 영역이다.

questions.passage: Being on the International Space Station (ISS) is a unique experience.  Astronauts live and work in microgravity, floating around instead of walking.  Researchers get to see Earth from a completely new perspective, and they get to work on important scientific research in conditions that are different from Earth's.  Many manufacturers are interested in manufacturing in space because the quality of a lot of products manufactured on Earth is influenced by temperature, pressure, radiation, and even the effects of gravity.  Creating good conditions for certain types of manufacturing on Earth requires the use of a lot of energy and resources, but those conditions occur naturally in space.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: 우주 제조의 조건.
det.analysis:
① 본문 'Astronauts live and work in microgravity, floating around instead of walking'과 일치해요

② 본문 'Many manufacturers are interested in manufacturing in space'와 일치해요

③ 본문 'Creating good conditions for certain types of manufacturing on Earth requires the use of a lot of energy and resources'에서 많은 에너지와 자원이 '든다'고 했어요. '들지 않는다'는 반대이므로 불일치예요 ← 정답

④ 본문 'the quality of a lot of products manufactured on Earth is influenced by temperature, pressure, radiation'과 일치해요
det.tip: Creating good conditions ~ requires a lot of energy and resources(많은 에너지와 자원이 든다)

ch: 우주비행사들은 미세중력 속에서 걷는 대신 떠다닌다.
많은 제조업체가 우주에서의 제조에 관심을 갖고 있다.
지구에서 좋은 제조 조건을 만드는 데는 많은 에너지와 자원이 들지 않는다.

questions.passage: The need to explore new frontiers like the Arctic and the American West may have been sparked by curiosity, but a major reason was to discover new resources.  Without new resources and technology, the Industrial Revolution of the 19th century would not have led to the rise of new industries and the growth of cities.  In the late 20th century, the Information Technology Revolution connected the world and transformed economies.  Now, it seems that space is the latest frontier for entrepreneurs to explore.  Finding new resources and exploring the unique environment are new opportunities for those who dare to take up the challenge.  The solar system is composed of many rocks floating in space.  The large ones are called planets, and the smaller ones are called asteroids.  Research has shown that asteroids contain valuable resources like gold and rare earth elements.  For example, one asteroid, 16 Psyche, is reported to consist mainly of gold and other precious metals, whose value is equal to billions of dollars per person on Earth.  From a space explorers' perspective, however, the most valuable resources from asteroids are neither valuable precious metals nor rare mineral deposits.  That valuable resource could actually be water, and it seems to have been overlooked because it doesn't seem as exciting as gold.  Water is expensive to transport into space due to its weight and volume.  Having a space station with sufficient water supplies in orbit around Earth would make space explorations much easier.  No one knows for sure what asteroid mining will look like, but it seems that robotic mining is most likely.  Robots will be sent to dig for target materials and send them back towards Earth.  They will be programmed to explore the surface and identify materials, and be equipped for tasks such as drilling, collecting, and transporting.  They may work independently or be controlled remotely from Earth.  Unfortunately, these types of robots have yet to be developed since the technology is still young.  As technology continues to develop, better methods for obtaining materials will undoubtedly emerge.  Being on the International Space Station (ISS) is a unique experience.  Astronauts live and work in microgravity, floating around instead of walking.  Researchers get to see Earth from a completely new perspective, and they get to work on important scientific research in conditions that are different from Earth's.  Many manufacturers are interested in manufacturing in space because the quality of a lot of products manufactured on Earth is influenced by temperature, pressure, radiation, and even the effects of gravity.  Creating good conditions for certain types of manufacturing on Earth requires the use of a lot of energy and resources, but those conditions occur naturally in space.  Drugs, beauty and food products, and advanced materials are all potential candidates to be tested and produced in space.  For example, without the effects of gravity, products that require a uniform quality like cosmetics would be easier to mix.  Other materials like 3D printed skin or muscle benefit from low pressure and gravity too.  Although the sun's radiation can be unhealthy for our skin, getting away from the protective effects of the atmosphere could also benefit the testing of products.  For example, fabrics and skin creams could be tested for their ability to protect against solar radiation.  Also, semiconductors and glass communication cables could be produced with higher purity and fewer faults.  Space technology has advanced greatly, and it seems that the cost of running a space program and improving it has decreased substantially since ambitious entrepreneurs have joined the adventure.  The conditions in space open up the possibility of manufacturing newer and better products.  Challenges remain, but it's not unreasonable to imagine sending a message from a device equipped with semiconductors that were produced in space.  The space project will ultimately reach a point where adventurous minds and their technological innovations will be able to travel safely to stars beyond the solar system.  The resources required to drive economic activity that have existed far beyond the reach of humanity are becoming much more reachable.  The question is no longer about how; it's about when.

❌ ② 결코 일어나지 않을 것: 'when(언제)'을 묻는다는 것은 반드시 일어난다는 전제라 반대예요

❌ ③ 비용이 가장 중요하다: 비용(how much)이 아니라 시기(when)를 말해요
